narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 67% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—roughly a two-in-three risk. That estimate was high enough that the school rejected the application.

The strongest reason was your undergraduate GPA of 2.80, which is below the 3.23 average among accepted students. In the ranking, this was the most influential factor, and it pushed the decision toward likely bar failure. The second most important factor was your first-year class-rank decile of 3, compared with an accepted-student average of 6; this relatively low early academic standing also pushed toward failure. Your LSAT score of 40 was the third most influential factor, but unlike the first two it pushed in your favor: it is above the accepted average of 37.18 and partially offset the academic concerns. Your gender and race were not used in this prediction.

To improve a future application, focus on the areas the review found concerning. Consider additional coursework or a structured post-baccalaureate record that demonstrates stronger academic performance, especially in writing- and reasoning-intensive subjects. You could also retake the LSAT to raise an already favorable score, seek admissions counseling about conditional or provisional pathways, and ask the school whether a delayed application with evidence of bar-readiness—such as prep coursework or legal work experience—would be viewed more competitively.
